what: The heuristic reconstructs the customer set, depot, visited facts, location facts, and directed routing costs once in new(). Costs come from grounded visit and return-to-depot operators via metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. Capacity and per-customer demands are used only when their complete exact numeric names survive translation; otherwise resource reasoning is safely disabled. For each state it finds the current location and unvisited customers, computes an MST routing bound, a degree-relaxation bound, an optional demand-weighted radial capacity bound, and a nearest-neighbor completion that inserts depot resets whenever no customer fits the remaining capacity. The returned estimate blends 70% of the greedy completion with 30% of the strongest structural bound, while never falling below that bound.
why: CVRP states are naturally characterized by the current route endpoint, the unvisited subset, and remaining vehicle capacity. The representative instances have metric-like but strongly clustered routing costs, so MST and degree relaxations capture global cluster connectivity while a nearest-neighbor rollout rewards locally coherent tours. Capacity can force expensive depot transitions, making a capacity-aware rollout and radial demand term valuable when the relevant fluents are available. The design remains useful when constants and demands are folded into derived expressions because its main routing estimate depends only on grounded operator costs and propositional state facts.
